Hidden chats disappear from your list in this app and open only after you enter the vault PIN. To hide a chat, long-press it and choose "Add to Vault" in the ⋮ menu. Turning this off asks for the PIN and brings all hidden chats back.

The vault PIN is separate from your device screen lock. This is a local lock in this app on this device, not encryption: hidden chats stay in your Telegram account and remain visible in other Telegram clients.

If you forget the PIN, you can get back in with a fingerprint (or another biometric your phone counts as strong; on many phones face unlock is not) as long as no fingerprint or face has been added or removed since you set the PIN, or with the Chat Lock master pincode, if that master was already set when you set the vault PIN (if you create the master later, change the vault PIN once to link them). The device screen lock is not accepted. Without one of these, a forgotten PIN cannot be recovered.

Hidden chats and Chat Lock stay on this device only — they do not transfer to a new device and have to be set up again there.
Open the vault by typing your PIN into chat search instead of holding the \"Chats\" title. Changing this setting asks for the vault PIN.

When on, there is no visible gesture: type your full vault PIN into the chat-list search and pause for a moment — the vault opens. If your vault uses a text password, type it and then tap Search.

Your own chats and contacts still appear while you type, but the text stays on this device: nothing is sent to Telegram's search until you tap Search. After several wrong codes, checking pauses for a while.

Increases the number of parallel connections and the size of file chunks. Higher settings open more parallel connections at once, so downloads are faster but your network activity becomes a more distinctive pattern to anyone observing your traffic. If your network can\'t handle the load, pick a lower option that suits your connection.

Keeps a copy of messages that others delete and marks it with 🗑. Stored only on this device and removed automatically after 30 days. Showing what they said is part of Zenlygram Pro.

Telegram doesn\'t say who deleted a message, so in private chats and small groups messages you delete for yourself on another device may also be kept. Not kept: your own messages, Saved Messages, service and self-destructing messages, deletions that also remove your messages (like clearing a chat), and chats where you can delete others\' messages. At most 5,000 messages are kept per account. Clearing Telegram\'s cache also permanently removes the media of kept messages. Long-press a kept message → Delete to remove it. Turning this off deletes all kept messages.

Zenlygram is an open-source Telegram client that respects your privacy and adds no ads or tracking of its own. Keeping it in step with Telegram\'s monthly updates takes time and hardware, and Zenlygram Pro is what pays for that work.\n\nEverything else in Zenlygram stays free.

When you start recording, send a message in the chat saying so, and play a short tone for you. It cannot put a sound into the call itself — the other person hears nothing new.

Recordings are created on this device and excluded from backups. They can leave it through Share or Saved Messages. Automatic sending is off by default. Saved Messages is a Telegram cloud chat: recordings sent there are stored on Telegram\'s servers and are not end-to-end encrypted. Recording another person may require their consent; you are responsible for obtaining it.

This records both sides of the call: your voice and the other person's. The recording is saved on this device.

Share exports a copy to the app or destination you choose. Sending to Saved Messages uploads it to Telegram's servers, where it is not end-to-end encrypted. Automatic sending happens only if you enable that setting.

Recording a conversation may require every participant's consent. You are responsible for obtaining any required consent before recording.
